summary: The root ضأن (DAn) primarily refers to sheep, specifically the fat-tailed kind. It denotes a single sheep or a flock, emphasizing their wool and meat.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: ضَأَنْتُ الضَّأْنَ I set apart the sheep [ from the goats]. (Az, TA, and K in art. معز.) One says, اِضْأَنْ ضَأْنَكَ وَٱمْعَزْ مَعْزَكَ Set apart thy sheep from the goats, and set apart thy goats from the sheep. (Az, TA.)
(S, M, K,) said of a man, (S,) or of a party of men, (M,) His, or their, ضَأْن [or sheep ] became numerous. (S, M, K.)

(S, M, Msb, K) and (S, M, K) and, (S, M, Msb, K,) which is also pronounced, with kesr to the first letter because of the kesr following, agreeably with a general rule applying to a word [of the measure فَعِيلٌ ] having any faucial letter [for its second radical], and and, which are mentioned by IAar, without ء, and therefore extr., (M,) [ Sheep; ] such as have wool, of what are termed غَنَم; one of which is called; (Msb;) [i. e.] they are pls., (S, K,) or [rather] quasi-pl.
A [ ring for the nose of a camel, such as is termed ] خِزَامَة, when made of sinew. (Sh, K.) [But see ضَانَةٌ, in art. ضون.]

is an extr., distorted, rel. n. [from ضَأْنٌ ]. (M.) You say مِعْزًى ضِئْنِيَّةٌ Goats that keep to the ضَأْن [or sheep ]. (M.) And سِقَآءٌ ضِئْنِىٌّ A wide, (M,) or large, (K,) skin, of the hide of a sheep, (M, K,) in which [ milk such as is termed ] رَائِب is churned. (K.)

: see ضَأْنٌ, in three places. It is also used as an epithet: one says كَبْشٌ ضَائِنٌ [app. meaning A ram: كَبْشٌ alone having several meanings]. (M.) And it signifies also (tropical:) Weak: (K, TA:) [opposed to مَاعِزٌ:] or a soft man, as though he were a ewe: (M, TA:) or one who ceases not to be goodly in body while a scanty eater: (M, K: *) or soft and flaccid in the belly. (M, K. *) And (assumed tropical:) Such as is white and broad, of sands. (K, TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
